transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is actually quite normal for plastics to remain wet in dishwashers like your Bosch Serie 4. Plastic holds very little heat during the wash, so it doesn't get hot enough to evaporate water droplets effectively; this is especially true on Eco programmes which use lower temperatures. However, if even glass and china are coming out cold and wet, or if you see heavy dripping, it often points to a drying aid issue. The most common fix is topping up the rinse aid, which helps water sheet off dishes rather than sitting in droplets. Could you check two things for me? First, is your rinse aid reservoir topped up? Second, when the cycle finishes, are the glasses and china still warm to the touch, or have they gone cold?
The rinse aid is empty, the symbol is lit on the display. I use all-in-one tablets though. The inside is hot and steamy when it finishes, I open the door straight away.

The empty rinse aid reservoir is the primary culprit here: rinse aid reduces surface tension so water sheets off dishes instead of beading up, which is essential for dry plastics and glass. Additionally, opening the door immediately releases the hot steam needed to evaporate remaining moisture from the interior surfaces. Please top up your rinse aid reservoir now. For your next wash, do not open the door until the cycle has completely finished and the machine has cooled down (often indicated by a specific light or just waiting 30–60 minutes). This combination of proper rinse aid levels and allowing full condensation drying should resolve the wetness.
